title: Resumable embedding importer with idempotent chunking and async job API
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: customers need a robust path to ingest large volumes of vectors with resumable uploads, strong dedup semantics, and predictable retry behavior. Current chunked streaming can lead to partial duplicates, inconsistent progress visibility, and hard-to-retry failures when network or worker errors occur. Goal: deliver a resumable streaming + bulk REST importer that provides per-chunk idempotency, ordered sequencing within uploads, explicit partial-commit semantics for low-latency availability, and an async job API for large batch processing. This work targets both hosted and Dedicated deployments and must be implementable in Private with minimal infra gaps.
acceptance_criteria: API: Support streaming gRPC and chunked REST upload that returns a stable job_id and per-chunk status summaries
Idempotency: Re-sending the same chunk (same session_id + chunk_sequence + chunk_checksum or idempotency_key) is a no-op and does not create duplicate vectors
Resumability: Clients can resume after interruptions by querying job state and uploading missing chunks; partial commits allow first N chunks to be queryable for reranking within 30s
Retries: Automatic transient retry policy for server-side ingestion failures with exponential backoff and client-observed retry headers
Observability: Job-level and chunk-level metrics exposed to Console (ingest throughput, bytes/sec, active sessions, duplicate suppression rate)
SLOs: Per-chunk acknowledgement latency median < 150ms, 95th percentile < 400ms under normal load; job finalization latency depends on size but progress is streaming
Backward compatibility: Existing single-call bulk embeddings API remains supported; new API is additive and opt-in
technical_design:
API surface:
  - POST /v1/embeddings/bulk -> creates a job, returns job_id and upload_url (chunked REST)
  - PATCH /v1/embeddings/bulk/{job_id}/chunks -> append chunk with headers: X-Session-Id, X-Chunk-Seq, X-Chunk-Checksum, Idempotency-Key
  - GET /v1/embeddings/bulk/{job_id} -> returns job state (PENDING, UPLOADING, PROCESSING, PARTIAL, COMPLETED, FAILED) and chunk map
  - gRPC streaming: client sends messages [session_id, seq, records[], checksum] and receives ack messages with seq and status

Session model: client supplies a session_id UUID per logical upload. Each chunk includes chunk_sequence (monotonic int) and SHA256 checksum. The server keeps a per-session manifest in durable metadata store (Postgres or Dynamo) listing chunks and their checksums and state.

Idempotency semantics: accept repeated chunk uploads as idempotent if session_id + chunk_sequence + checksum match existing manifest entry. If sequence matches but checksum differs, mark session as corrupted and require client to re-create session (safety to avoid silent divergence). Support optional client-provided Idempotency-Key for cross-session dedupe (string).

Storage pipeline: incoming chunks are written to object storage (S3/GCS) with path: {tenant}/{job_id}/chunks/{seq}. Each chunk upload triggers a lightweight verification task that updates the manifest and emits an event to the processing queue. A processing pool picks up verified chunks in sequence to create embeddings in the vector store. We separate upload from indexing to make partial results available quickly.

Partial commit & visibility: after N contiguous chunks are processed, update job state to PARTIAL and publish per-chunk vector availability. Clients can poll job or subscribe to webhook when first partial commit completes, enabling early reranking without waiting for full job completion.

Exactly-once vs at-least-once trade-off: we enforce strong dedupe at ingestion using item-level idempotency tokens when present (client-provided), plus checksum+sequence for session-level exactly-once. In rare mismatch cases we prefer safety (reject/abort session) rather than risk silent duplicates.

Scaling & performance: chunk sizes tuned (default 1MB..10MB) to balance serialization overhead and parallelism. Processing pipeline supports parallel chunk processing across independent chunks but maintains ordered indexing per-session where ordering requested. Autoscaling rules: scale indexer workers by pending_chunks and CPU/GP mem; target throughput 500K vectors/hour per cluster node for initial rollout.

Failure modes & recovery: server-side transient errors retried with jitter; permanent corruption marks chunk/ session FAILED and surfaces detailed error. A manual "repair" flow allows operator to re-import specific chunk blobs and resume processing after verification.

Storage and retention: chunk blobs retained for 7 days by default and longer with customer-configurable retention policy to support reclaim/repair flows. Manifest entries are compacted into an indexable job summary after completion.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy API behind feature flag for 10% of new ingest traffic; monitor duplicate suppression, ack latencies, and storage costs
Phase 2 (tenant pilots): enable for 5 pilot customers migrating large datasets (>100K vectors) and gather feedback on resume UX and partial-commit timing
Phase 3 (general availability): enable by default with migration docs and SDK convenience wrappers (Python/TS) that implement session resume and chunk checksumming
Rollback: revert feature flag and surface queued chunks for manual backfill if an unrecoverable bug is detected
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest state machine and idempotency logic (duplicate chunk, checksum mismatch, sequence gaps)
Integration tests: end-to-end upload -> partial commit -> finalization on staging with mocked object storage and vector DB
Chaos tests: induce network drops mid-upload to validate resume correctness and no-duplicate guarantees
Performance tests: validation harness to saturate chunk uploads and measure median/95th ack latency and indexer backpressure behavior
Security tests: verify tenant isolation for chunk storage paths, validate signed upload URLs and request auth
notes: Design review 2026-03-05 notes: prefer session-level manifests in Postgres for strong transactional updates (vs eventual consistency in Redis). Consider using changefeeds to trigger processing workers.
PM feedback: prioritize clear SDK helpers for resume flow; provide a high-level convenience function that hides chunking and idempotency tokens from customers.
Design decision: Require checksum on each chunk to simplify corruption detection; this increases client CPU but dramatically reduces ambiguous retries.
